The most potent compounds in this series appear to share a specific scaffold involving a fused bicyclic aromatic system (likely a pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine or similar core) linked to an acrylamide Michael acceptor, as evidenced by the high potency of the top hits (8.44, 7.58, 6.94) which contain both features, while lower potency compounds lack one or both. The top hit (8.44) contains a fused bicyclic aromatic system and a Michael acceptor. The second hit (7.58) lacks the fused bicyclic system but has the Michael acceptor. The third hit (6.94) lacks the Michael acceptor but has the fused bicyclic system. However, the drop in potency is significant when either feature is removed or when the scaffold changes to simple monocycles. The most potent compounds seem to require the fused bicyclic aromatic core combined with the Michael acceptor functionality to achieve high affinity. Therefore, we should constrain the library to compounds containing both the fused bicyclic aromatic system and the Michael acceptor.
